images.title: Ones become Tenths
images.purpose: Show 1325 ÷ 4 = 331.25 on a place value chart, with the leftover One regrouped into Tenths and Tenths into Hundredths.
images.composition: A five column place value chart in the centre holding the quotient, with the dividing sum above it and two regrouping arrows below the right hand columns; wide white margins.
exact_structure: Chart: 5 columns with headers Hundreds, Tens, Ones, Tenths, Hundredths; Hundreds, Tens and Ones headers teal #0072B2, Tenths and Hundredths headers amber #E69F00.
A thick reddish purple #CC79A7 decimal point sits on the line between the Ones and Tenths columns.
Quotient row digits: 3 under Hundreds, 3 under Tens, 1 under Ones, 2 under Tenths, 5 under Hundredths.

Below the chart: a reddish purple #CC79A7 curved arrow from under the Ones column to under the Tenths column labelled 1 One = 10 Tenths, and a second arrow from under the Tenths column to under the Hundredths column labelled 2 Tenths = 20 Hundredths.
rejection: quotient digits other than 3, 3, 1, 2, 5 in that column order
the decimal point not between Ones and Tenths
more or fewer than 2 regrouping arrows
images.takeaway: When Ones are left over, regroup them as Tenths and keep sharing, putting the point in the quotient at that moment.
images.description: A place value chart showing the quotient 331.25 for 1325 ÷ 4, with arrows showing 1 One regrouped as 10 Tenths and 2 Tenths regrouped as 20 Hundredths.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on 1324 ÷ 4 and 1325 ÷ 4.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to follow the arrows from left to right and notice that the point appears exactly where Ones turn into Tenths.

image_decisions.why: Regrouping into Tenths and Hundredths is clearest on a place value chart.
